absent: dmirror open, release and ioctl command dispatch beyond the visible tail
dmirror chunk allocation, removal and free page reclamation helpers
backing page accessor and device or chunk lookup helpers
optional coherent device address parameters and initial chunk sizing
fault allocation copy helper and device selection policy
identifier allocator implementation and shared instance definition
handover core preserve, unpreserve, restore and subtree semantics
device tree construction and query helper error behavior
remainder of handover initialization after the enabled check
exact numeric error codes for ioctl, mapping and migration failures

findings.text: User command record holds five 64 bit slots describing a target address known as addr, a user pointer known as ptr, a requested count known as npages, a completed count known as cpages, and a fault tally known as faults. The same layout serves every mirror operation.

Ten user operations share magic letter H with sequential numbers zero through nine covering read, write, migration to device, migration to system, snapshot, exclusive, check exclusive, release, flags query and unlocked read. One allocation failure flag occupies the lowest bit.

Protection annotation is a single byte. Marker known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_ERROR takes two hundred fifty five and marker known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_NONE takes zero. Markers known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_READ and HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_WRITE take one and two. Markers known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_PMD, HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_PUD and HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_ZERO take four, eight and sixteen. Private markers known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_DEV_PRIVATE_LOCAL and HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_DEV_PRIVATE_REMOTE take thirty two and forty eight. Coherent markers known as HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_DEV_COHERENT_LOCAL and HMM_DMIRROR_PROT_DEV_COHERENT_REMOTE take sixty four and eighty.
Memory classification reserves zero for uninitialized use. Marker known as HMM_DMIRROR_MEMORY_DEVICE_PRIVATE takes one and marker known as HMM_DMIRROR_MEMORY_DEVICE_COHERENT takes two.
Handover test identity uses a four byte magic whose hexadecimal form reads 4B484F21 matching letters K H O with exclamation, a subtree name kho_test and a compatibility string kho-test-v1.

Handover test state aggregates counts and arrays for generated folios alongside preservation metadata and verification data. Individual members are known as nr_folios and folios for the collection, folios_info with preservation record known as folios_info_phys for physical descriptions, preserved tally known as nr_folios_preserved, descriptive folio known as fdt, and checksum known as csum. A single static instance backs the whole test.

A character device family exposes open, release, mapping, control and seek behavior through a common operations table known as dmirror_fops owned by the test module. Mapping populates the requested range while control multiplexes the mirror commands.

Device memory callbacks provide release, migration to system memory on fault, and folio split handling through a pagemap operations table known as dmirror_devmem_ops. These hooks integrate simulated device memory with migration and split machinery.

Entries known as hmm_dmirror_init and hmm_dmirror_exit manage module lifetime. Load creates a character region and instantiates two private mirrors plus two coherent mirrors when both optional addresses are supplied. Unload tears down every instantiated device and releases the region, with load unwinding already created devices on failure.

Driver known as ida_checks executes the full identifier allocator check sequence on a shared instance, reports how many assertions passed from how many run, and signals overall outcome through its return value. An empty exit hook known as ida_exit accompanies it.

Handover testing offers save side generation plus preservation with descriptive metadata, and restore side validation of identity, sizes, per folio order and checksum. Initialization first consults whether handover is enabled.
A spin based guard inside each mirror device serializes updates to the free count and to the two free lists during memory release. A separate mutex is initialized per device alongside the spin guard.

Mapping guarantees each page slot in the requested interval ends backed by a newly allocated zeroed page that is inserted into the callers address space. Failure of allocation or insertion aborts the operation and releases the page at fault without leaking earlier insertions.

Release distinguishes backing storage from the device page itself, freeing the former by its order when distinct. The device page returns to an order appropriate free pool with an incremented free tally unless its chunk is being removed.

Fault migration works on a range aligned down to the faulting folio size, reduced to a single page when a page table entry shows partial mapping. Sizing of temporary collections follows the final range, and distinct fault codes report resource exhaustion versus invalid setup while always releasing temporaries.

Splitting derives the tail backing page by offset from the head backing base, carries over the mirror association, clears compound state, and initializes mapping and reference state for both sides. Null backing or null tail produce defined degenerate handling instead of offset propagation.

Allocator checks expect dense increasing assignment from zero, reuse of recently freed low values before growth beyond the prior high water, and emptiness after destruction. Destroying an empty instance is idempotent, and single element destroy cycles are exercised across representative bases including edge and large sparse values.

Leaf, boundary and conversion checks require full bitmap sized runs from varied bases to allocate densely and return to empty after teardown, exhaustion to be signaled when filling past the high address limit for geometrically growing sizes, and stable behavior across bitmap and word size transitions.

Misuse checks verify that freeing never allocated identifiers across empty, single value, single bitmap and tree shapes is tolerated with warnings, and that existence plus first search honor empty versus populated states with proper not found and invalid range signaling.

Preservation stores each folio as combined physical address plus order in a preserved array, accompanied by folio count, checksum and identity metadata in a descriptive tree. Restoration rejects mismatched magic, compatibility, property sizes, missing entries, order divergence or checksum inequality.

Data generation fills allocations up to a configurable ceiling without exceeding it, choosing random orders and shrinking the final order to fit, filling each folio with random bytes while accumulating a checksum. Allocation failure discards all prior folios and reports resource exhaustion.

Device lifecycle moves from number assignment and primitive initialization through naming and initial chunk provisioning to live character device exposure. Any failure before liveness releases the device reference, while removal always deletes the character linkage before dropping the final reference.

Preservation proceeds through descriptive folio allocation, data preservation, metadata formatting and tree insertion, with each later failure unwinding only the earlier stages already completed, ensuring no preserved folio or array leaks on error paths.

The suite advances from an initial emptiness assertion through allocation, destruction, leaf, limit, conversion, misuse and search phases in fixed order, accumulating run and pass tallies throughout and emitting a summary at the end.

The suite driver return polarity appears inverted, yielding success when tallies diverge and an error when they match, which risks misreporting overall outcome to module loading. Misuse tests deliberately emit warnings that must be ignored when judging logs.

Fault handling must tolerate allocation failure, setup rejection and partial mapping without leaking temporaries or leaving migrations half finalized. Split handling must not dereference absent backing when head lacks association and must reset order and mapping when no tail is supplied.

Restore trusts physical descriptions from preserved storage and must validate every property length, address alignment via masking, order match and checksum equality before use, releasing each restored folio and the array even on mid loop failure.
User header employs a single inclusion guard macro to ensure idempotent inclusion across translation units.
Failure diagnostics use an intentionally empty dump helper, so assertion failures surface through generic stack traces rather than allocator specific output.
Test logging prefixes every message with the module name through a format wrapper macro.
